summary: This article explains how rotation, timing, communication, and the physics of a good serve or spike make volleyball a team sport built on science.
introduce: Show the title “Volleyball: Teamwork in the Air” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: the direction or slant at which something moves or meets something else
choosing exactly the right moment to do something
a turn, in which people or things move around in order

challengeTerms.def: the curved path an object follows as it moves through the air
a forward spin given to a ball that makes it dip or curve downward
the speed of something in a certain direction

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that good teamwork matters more than individual skill in sports? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how two different science ideas from the article help a team score a point.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review angle, timing, and rotation, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses trajectory, topspin, and velocity to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
